title: Pelling vs Yuksom vs Uttarey: where to base
meta_description: Pelling, Yuksom or Uttarey? Altitude, Kangchenjunga views, rooms, prices and day trips compared, so you pick the right West Sikkim base for your trip.
summary: Base in Pelling for Kangchenjunga views, the most rooms and easy sightseeing; in Yuksom for history, quiet and the Goecha La trail; in Uttarey for forest, birds and village life near the Nepal border. Most first visits work best as two nights in Pelling and two in Yuksom, adding Uttarey on a second trip.

sections.heading: Three bases, three different trips
paras: West Sikkim, now Gyalshing district, is small on the map and slow on the road. Pelling, Yuksom and Uttarey are all within about 35–40 km of each other, but the hill roads between them average 20–25 km/h, so each is 1.5–2.5 hours from the others. Where you sleep decides what you see at dawn, how long you sit in a car and how much you pay.

We send travellers to all three every season. The short version: Pelling is the viewing gallery, Yuksom is the history book and the trailhead, and Uttarey is the village in the forest. The table puts the practical differences side by side. Distances and prices are indicative: check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Pelling: the view and the convenience
paras: Pelling sits on a ridge at about 2,150 m, with Kabru, Rathong, Kangchenjunga and Pandim lined up to the north on clear mornings. It has the widest range of rooms in the district, from ₹1,500 doubles to premium hotels, and the town's taxi stand runs fixed-rate tours to almost everything worth seeing in the west.

Within walking distance you have Pemayangtse Monastery, Sikkim's leading Nyingma monastery, founded as a small temple by Lhatsun Chenpo in the 1640s and enlarged in 1705, and the Rabdentse ruins, the second capital of the kingdom from 1670. Sanga Choeling Monastery (1697) and the Chenrezig statue with its glass skywalk sit on the ridge above. Khecheopalri Lake, Rimbi waterfall and Kanchenjunga Falls are half-day car trips.

The downside is that Pelling is a hotel town. Many buildings are recent concrete, the main road is busy with tourist cars from October to December, and prices jump in holiday weeks. If you want a village feel, sleep in Darap, 7 km below, and drive up for the views.
list: Choose Pelling if this is your first trip to Sikkim, if you are travelling with children or elderly parents, or if the mountain view is the main point.
Stay two or three nights: one clear morning is never guaranteed.

sections.heading: Yuksom: history and the trailhead
paras: Yuksom, at about 1,780 m and roughly 35 km north of Pelling, is where the Namgyal kingdom of Sikkim began. Tradition holds that three lamas crowned Phuntsog Namgyal as the first Chogyal here in 1642, at the stone seats of Norbugang. The name is usually explained as the meeting place of the three learned monks. Dubdi Monastery, traditionally dated to 1701 and often called the oldest in Sikkim, is a 45–60 minute climb through forest above the village, and Kathok Lake sits at its edge.

Yuksom is also the trailhead for Dzongri and Goecha La in Khangchendzonga National Park, so in April–May and October–November you share the village with trekking groups. Outside those weeks it is one of the quietest places we know in Sikkim: one main street, prayer flags, cardamom fields below and the sound of the Rathong Chu.

Rooms are fewer and simpler than in Pelling, with good mid-range lodges and family homestays. Tashiding Monastery, one of the holiest in Sikkim, is about 19 km away, so Yuksom makes a natural second base on a monastery trip.
list: Choose Yuksom for history, monasteries, short forest walks or a trek.
Two nights lets you see Dubdi, Norbugang and Kathok Lake on foot and Tashiding by car.

sections.heading: Uttarey: forest, birds and a border village
paras: Uttarey, at about 2,000 m, lies at the far western edge of Sikkim, roughly 35 km by road from Pelling through Dentam. The road crosses the Singshore Bridge, a long suspension span high above a gorge, then climbs into thick forest of oak, magnolia and rhododendron. The village is a mix of Limbu, Bhutia and Nepali-speaking families, and the Gyalshing district administration lists the Chewabhanjyang pass on the Nepal border about 10 km beyond.

There is little to tick off in Uttarey, which is the point. Days are for walking forest trails, watching birds at dawn, visiting the small monastery above the village and eating at a homestay table. In March–April the rhododendrons on the ridges towards the Singalila range bloom. Rooms are homestays and small lodges, about ₹1,200–2,000 per person with meals.

The trade-offs are distance and simplicity. Uttarey is 6.5–7.5 hours from NJP, mobile signal can be patchy and hot water may come in a bucket. It suits people who already know Pelling or who want a slow, walking trip.

sections.heading: How we usually split the nights
paras: For a first trip of four or five nights in the west, we suggest two or three nights in Pelling and two in Yuksom. You see the mountain from the best viewpoints, walk the monasteries and history sites at an easy pace, and avoid sitting in a car every day. A six or seven-night trip can add two nights in Uttarey or Hee Bermiok on the way back.

If you are combining the west with Gangtok, Pelling is the obvious stop because the Gangtok–Pelling road via Ravangla and Legship takes about 5–6 hours. Yuksom from Gangtok is a long day, closer to 7 hours, so do it after Pelling rather than straight from the capital.
list: 3 nights: Pelling only, with a half-day to Khecheopalri Lake.
Trekking: Pelling 1 to acclimatise, then Yuksom before the trail.

sections.heading: Getting around from each base
paras: From Pelling, almost everything is a half-day trip. The taxi stand's fixed-rate tours cover Khecheopalri Lake, Rimbi and Kanchenjunga Falls, and the town sights, for roughly ₹2,500–3,500 in a small car. Shared jeeps to Gyalshing run all day, and from Gyalshing you can reach Jorethang, Legship, Tashiding and Yuksom.

From Yuksom, most of what you came for is on foot: Norbugang and Kathok Lake are in the village, Dubdi is a climb above it, and the Khangchendzonga National Park gate is at the top of the street. For Tashiding or Khecheopalri you need a car, roughly ₹2,000–3,000 for a half-day return. Shared jeeps leave for Gyalshing early in the morning and return in the afternoon, so plan any day trip around them.

From Uttarey, transport is the weak point. A few shared jeeps run to Gyalshing and Jorethang in the morning, and cars are best booked through your homestay the evening before. We usually keep the same car and driver for the Uttarey leg so you are not stranded if the weather turns.

sections.heading: Season changes the answer
paras: From mid-October to December, Pelling's view justifies its prices and crowds. In January and February, Pelling can be cold (dawn around 2–5 °C) and Uttarey colder, while Yuksom is a little milder at its lower altitude. In March and April, Uttarey and the trail above Yuksom are at their best for flowers. In the June–September monsoon all three are green and cloudy, and the road to Uttarey is the most prone to slides; we keep monsoon trips to Pelling and Yuksom, with buffer time. Check current status before you travel.
One more rule of thumb: whatever the month, give yourself a spare morning in Pelling. Cloud often lifts for an hour after dawn and closes by 9 am, and two chances at the view are far better than one.

faqs.q: Is Pelling or Yuksom better for a first trip?
faqs.a: Pelling, for most first visits. It has the clearest Kangchenjunga views, the most rooms in every price band and a taxi stand that runs tours to the main sights. Yuksom is quieter and richer in history but has fewer rooms and only partial mountain views. Ideally do both: two or three nights in Pelling, then two in Yuksom.

faqs.q: How far is Yuksom from Pelling?
faqs.a: About 35 km by road, roughly 1.5–2 hours by car via Rimbi and Kanchenjunga Falls. Shared jeeps run from Gyalshing to Yuksom for about ₹100–200 a seat, and a reserved small car from Pelling costs roughly ₹2,500–3,500 one way. Monsoon slides can slow the road, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I see Kangchenjunga from Yuksom?
faqs.a: Only partly from the village itself, because ridges block much of the range. You get better views from the climb to Dubdi Monastery and from higher points around Yuksom, and the full panorama only from Dzongri on the trek. If seeing the range is your priority, plan your clear-morning nights in Pelling.

Yes, if you enjoy forest, birds and quiet village life more than sightseeing. Uttarey sits at about 2,000 m near the Nepal border, with oak and rhododendron forest, a small monastery, Singshore Bridge on the approach and homestay meals. It is a long way from NJP, about 6.5–7.5 hours, so give it at least two nights.

faqs.q: Where should I stay in West Sikkim with elderly parents?
faqs.a: Pelling. It has hotels with lifts or ground-floor rooms, the main sights are short drives or gentle walks away, and the altitude of about 2,150 m is comfortable for most healthy older travellers. Avoid long same-day drives: break the trip from NJP into easy stages and keep one free half-day. Yuksom works as a second base for an easy pace.

faqs.q: Which base is best for trekking in West Sikkim?
faqs.a: Yuksom, because it is the trailhead for Dzongri and Goecha La and the place where Khangchendzonga National Park permits, guides and porters are arranged. Uttarey is the base for walks towards the Singalila ridge. We suggest one night in Pelling or Yuksom before any trek to rest after the long drive from the plains.

In mid-October to December and in the Bengal holiday weeks around Durga Puja and New Year, Upper Pelling gets busy with tourist cars and full hotels. The rest of the year it is a calm small town. If you want quiet in peak season, sleep in Darap below Pelling or base yourself in Yuksom.

faqs.q: How many nights do I need in West Sikkim?
faqs.a: Three nights covers Pelling and its nearby sights. Five nights lets you add Yuksom at an easy pace, and seven nights adds Uttarey or Hee Bermiok. Remember that the drive from NJP or Bagdogra takes 5–7 hours each way, so the first and last days are mostly travel.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Pelling, Yuksom or Uttarey?
faqs.a: Indian citizens do not need permits for these three villages; you only pay Sikkim's ₹50 tourist entry fee at your hotel. Foreign nationals need a Restricted Area Permit for Sikkim through the e-FRRO portal. Treks into Khangchendzonga National Park from Yuksom need separate permits for everyone. Check current status before you travel.
